verdict.rationale: Column's docs name its account types: FDIC-insured accounts opened on behalf of customers, with FBO, sweep, clearing and custom types. They also cover storing customer funds in an FBO account, two-legged pass-through flows, and custom roles that limit access down to specific bank accounts. Reports and statements give ledger visibility, so the structure is partly transparent. Missing for 10: plain documentation of where FDIC insurance actually attaches (e.g. pass-through coverage for FBO pools versus individual accounts), an explicit explanation of pooled versus per-customer account trade-offs, a clear statement of who can view the underlying ledger, and independent corroboration.
